subject.title: fix(cron): bound misconfigured timeoutSeconds/noOutputTimeoutSeconds to default

question: Should an explicit `0` for command-cron timeout fields remain the supported no-timeout value, or should it become an unset value that falls back to the default?
rationale: Current code gives zero an explicit unbounded interpretation, while current public docs only establish the default when the field is absent; choosing a new meaning for stored zero values is a compatibility policy decision.

options.title: Keep zero as no timeout
options.body: Retain the existing zero behavior and separately handle only invalid negative or non-finite values if a bounded repair is still needed.

options.title: Retire zero semantics safely
options.body: Treat zero as unset only with a documented upgrade path, a doctor/config migration or validation error, and fresh-install plus upgrade proof.

recommendation.title: Keep zero as no timeout
recommendation.body: Retain the existing zero behavior and separately handle only invalid negative or non-finite values if a bounded repair is still needed.
